title: The Wright brothers make the first powered flight
clues: This breakthrough changed how people could travel across the world.
It took place on a windy stretch of sand in the United States.
Two bicycle makers had spent years testing wings and controls.
The machine stayed airborne for only 12 seconds on its first attempt.
Orville Wright piloted the Wright Flyer near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.
explanation: Orville Wright flew the Wright Flyer for 12 seconds near Kitty Hawk, making the first controlled, sustained flight of a powered, heavier-than-air aircraft.

title: The Panama Canal opens to traffic
clues: This engineering project shortened a major global trade route.
Its construction reshaped land between two oceans.
Workers used a system of locks to raise and lower ships.
The route removed the need to sail around Cape Horn.
The cargo ship SS Ancon made the first official transit of the Panama Canal.
explanation: The SS Ancon completed the first official passage through the Panama Canal, opening the waterway to commercial traffic between the Atlantic and Pacific.

title: The Nineteenth Amendment is certified
clues: This legal milestone expanded democratic participation in the United States.
It followed decades of organizing, petitions, and public demonstrations.
Tennessee supplied the final state ratification needed shortly beforehand.
The change prohibited denying the vote on the basis of sex.
The Nineteenth Amendment was formally certified as part of the US Constitution.
explanation: US Secretary of State Bainbridge Colby certified the Nineteenth Amendment, constitutionally protecting women's right to vote across the United States.

title: The entrance to Tutankhamun's tomb is discovered
clues: This archaeological discovery renewed worldwide fascination with an ancient civilization.
It happened after years of searching in a royal burial ground.
A water carrier reportedly noticed a step beneath the sand.
Howard Carter's team uncovered a staircase bearing intact seals.
The find led into the tomb of the Egyptian pharaoh Tutankhamun.
explanation: Howard Carter's excavation team found the first step leading to Tutankhamun's tomb in Egypt's Valley of the Kings. The sealed doorway was reached later that month.

title: The first Winter Olympic Games open
clues: This international competition established a new stage for cold-weather sport.
Athletes from 16 nations took part in its first edition.
Events included skating, skiing, ice hockey, and bobsleigh.
The host town sat beneath Mont Blanc in the French Alps.
The first Winter Olympics opened in Chamonix, France.
explanation: The International Winter Sports Week opened in Chamonix and was later recognized as the first Olympic Winter Games.

title: John Logie Baird demonstrates television
clues: This demonstration previewed a medium that would transform news and entertainment.
The early apparatus used spinning mechanical discs rather than modern electronics.
Members of the Royal Institution attended the event in London.
Viewers saw moving images with recognizable light and shade.
John Logie Baird gave one of the first public demonstrations of television.
explanation: Scottish inventor John Logie Baird demonstrated a working mechanical television system to members of the Royal Institution in London.

title: Charles Lindbergh completes a solo Atlantic flight
clues: This journey proved the growing reach of long-distance aviation.
One pilot traveled alone for more than 33 hours.
The aircraft carried extra fuel but no front windshield.
The flight began near New York and ended before a huge European crowd.
Charles Lindbergh landed the Spirit of St. Louis in Paris.
explanation: Charles Lindbergh landed at Le Bourget Field outside Paris, completing the first nonstop solo flight across the Atlantic Ocean.

title: Alexander Fleming discovers penicillin
clues: This accidental observation helped begin a revolution in medicine.
A researcher returned from holiday to inspect contaminated laboratory dishes.
Bacteria would not grow close to a particular mould.
The substance was named after the Penicillium mould that produced it.
Alexander Fleming recorded the antibacterial effect that led to penicillin.
explanation: Alexander Fleming noticed that Penicillium mould inhibited bacteria in a culture dish, the observation that led to the development of penicillin antibiotics.

title: The first Academy Awards ceremony is held
clues: This gathering began one of the entertainment industry's best-known traditions.
The first ceremony was a private dinner rather than a televised spectacle.
Only about 270 guests attended at a Hollywood hotel.
Winners had been announced before the event began.
The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences presented its first Oscars.
explanation: The first Academy Awards were presented during a banquet at the Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel, honoring films released in 1927 and 1928.

title: Gandhi begins the Salt March
clues: This nonviolent campaign challenged colonial rule through an everyday necessity.
A small group began a journey that grew into a national movement.
The march covered roughly 390 kilometres across western India.
Its destination was the Arabian Sea coast at Dandi.
Mahatma Gandhi left Sabarmati Ashram to protest the British salt monopoly.
explanation: Mahatma Gandhi and 78 followers left Sabarmati Ashram for Dandi, beginning the Salt March and a wider campaign of civil disobedience against British rule.

title: The Empire State Building opens
clues: This structure became an instant symbol of a modern city.
It rose during the Great Depression at remarkable speed.
For decades it held the title of the world's tallest building.
A ceremonial button in Washington switched on its lights.
The Empire State Building officially opened in New York City.
explanation: President Herbert Hoover remotely switched on the Empire State Building's lights as the 102-story New York skyscraper officially opened.

title: The Golden Gate Bridge opens to pedestrians
clues: This opening connected communities across a famously difficult stretch of water.
Its towers and cables became an icon of twentieth-century engineering.
Strong currents, fog, and wind complicated construction.
The first day was reserved for people crossing on foot.
The Golden Gate Bridge opened between San Francisco and Marin County.
explanation: Around 200,000 people crossed the Golden Gate Bridge on foot during Pedestrian Day, one day before it opened to vehicle traffic.

title: Indonesia proclaims independence
clues: This declaration established a new nation after centuries of colonial rule.
It was delivered shortly after the end of a major global conflict in Asia.
The text was brief and read before a crowd in Jakarta.
Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta signed the proclamation.
The Republic of Indonesia declared its independence.
explanation: Sukarno read the Proclamation of Indonesian Independence in Jakarta, with Mohammad Hatta as co-signatory, beginning the country's struggle for internationally recognized sovereignty.

title: The United Nations officially comes into existence
clues: This institution was created to support international peace and cooperation.
Its founding agreement was negotiated as a global war came to an end.
The organization began when enough member states ratified its charter.
Its headquarters would later be built in New York City.
The Charter of the United Nations entered into force.
explanation: The United Nations officially came into existence when its Charter was ratified by the required signatories, including the five permanent Security Council members.

sources.label: United Nations — History of the UN

title: ENIAC is formally dedicated
clues: This machine marked a major step toward general-purpose electronic computing.
It filled a large room and used thousands of vacuum tubes.
Its first programmers included a pioneering team of women.
The machine was built at the University of Pennsylvania.
ENIAC was formally dedicated and presented as an electronic numerical computer.
explanation: The University of Pennsylvania formally dedicated ENIAC, one of the earliest general-purpose electronic digital computers.

title: India becomes independent
clues: This transition ended nearly two centuries of British colonial rule.
It followed a long movement that included mass nonviolent resistance.
A new prime minister addressed the nation at midnight.
The speech became known as Tryst with Destiny.
Jawaharlal Nehru marked the independence of India.
explanation: India became an independent dominion, and Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru delivered his Tryst with Destiny speech as power transferred from British rule.

title: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights is adopted
clues: This document set out a shared international standard for human dignity.
It was drafted in the aftermath of a devastating world conflict.
Representatives from many legal and cultural traditions shaped its articles.
Eleanor Roosevelt chaired the commission behind the text.
The UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
explanation: The United Nations General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in Paris, setting out 30 fundamental rights and freedoms.

title: Mount Everest is climbed for the first confirmed time
clues: This achievement reached the highest point on Earth.
The expedition approached through Nepal and used bottled oxygen.
News of the success reached London around the time of a royal coronation.
A New Zealand beekeeper and a Nepalese-Indian mountaineer made the final climb.
Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reached the summit of Mount Everest.
explanation: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay became the first climbers confirmed to have reached the summit of Mount Everest.

title: Brown v. Board of Education is decided
clues: This court ruling challenged legalized segregation in public life.
Several cases from different US states were considered together.
The decision rejected the idea that separate schools could be equal.
Chief Justice Earl Warren delivered a unanimous opinion.
The US Supreme Court decided Brown v. Board of Education.
explanation: The US Supreme Court unanimously ruled that racial segregation in public schools violated the Constitution's Equal Protection Clause.

sources.label: US National Archives — Brown v. Board

title: CERN is established
clues: This organization was created to rebuild scientific collaboration across Europe.
Its work focuses on the smallest known building blocks of matter.
Its main laboratory straddles the border between Switzerland and France.
It would later operate the world's largest particle accelerator.
The convention establishing CERN entered into force.
explanation: The convention creating the European Organization for Nuclear Research entered into force, formally establishing CERN.

title: The Bandung Conference opens
clues: This meeting gave newly independent nations a stronger collective voice.
Delegates came from 29 countries across two continents.
Discussion focused on colonialism, development, peace, and cooperation.
The gathering helped lay foundations for the Non-Aligned Movement.
The Asian-African Conference opened in Bandung, Indonesia.
explanation: Leaders and representatives from 29 Asian and African countries gathered in Bandung for a landmark conference on cooperation and opposition to colonialism.

title: Ghana becomes independent
clues: This event accelerated a wider wave of African decolonization.
The country had previously been known as the Gold Coast.
Its new flag used red, gold, green, and a black star.
Kwame Nkrumah became the new nation's first prime minister.
Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence from European rule.
explanation: Ghana gained independence from Britain under the leadership of Kwame Nkrumah, becoming a powerful symbol for African liberation movements.

title: Sputnik 1 is launched
clues: This small object changed scientific competition between global powers.
Its radio signal could be heard by listeners around the world.
The polished metal sphere completed an orbit in roughly 96 minutes.
Its launch began the Space Age and intensified the space race.
The Soviet Union placed Sputnik 1 into Earth orbit.
explanation: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite to orbit Earth, opening the Space Age.

sources.label: NASA — Sputnik and the dawn of the Space Age

title: NASA begins operations
clues: This new agency consolidated a nation's civilian space research.
It inherited staff and facilities from an aeronautics organization.
Its creation followed the launch of the first artificial satellite.
It would later lead the Mercury, Gemini, and Apollo programs.
The National Aeronautics and Space Administration began work.
explanation: NASA officially began operations, absorbing the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics and taking charge of the United States' civilian space program.

title: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space
clues: This journey expanded human exploration beyond Earth for the first time.
The traveler completed one orbit in less than two hours.
The spacecraft was controlled mostly from the ground.
The mission's call sign was Kedr, meaning cedar.
Yuri Gagarin flew aboard Vostok 1.
explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin completed one orbit of Earth aboard Vostok 1, becoming the first human to travel into space.

title: The March on Washington takes place
clues: This mass gathering called for jobs, freedom, and equal rights.
More than 200,000 people assembled in the US capital.
The event took place between the Washington Monument and Lincoln Memorial.
It became closely associated with a speech about a dream.
Martin Luther King Jr. addressed the March on Washington.
explanation: The March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom brought a vast crowd to the Lincoln Memorial, where Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his I Have a Dream speech.

sources.label: US National Park Service — March on Washington

title: The Beatles appear on The Ed Sullivan Show
clues: This television appearance became a landmark in popular culture.
An audience of more than 70 million watched in the United States.
The performers had recently arrived from the United Kingdom.
They opened with All My Loving before a studio full of screaming fans.
The Beatles made their first live US television appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show.
explanation: The Beatles performed live on The Ed Sullivan Show, a broadcast widely remembered as the moment Beatlemania reached a mass American audience.

sources.label: The Ed Sullivan Show — The Beatles

title: The first human heart transplant is performed
clues: This operation opened a new era in transplant medicine.
A large surgical team worked through the night in Cape Town.
The recipient was a grocer suffering from severe heart disease.
The surgeon leading the operation was Christiaan Barnard.
Groote Schuur Hospital carried out the first human-to-human heart transplant.
explanation: Christiaan Barnard led the team that transplanted a human heart into Louis Washkansky at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town.

sources.label: Groote Schuur Hospital — Heart of Cape Town Museum

title: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon
clues: This mission carried human exploration to another world.
Three astronauts traveled aboard a command module named Columbia.
Two crew members descended in a smaller craft named Eagle.
The landing site was in the Sea of Tranquility.
Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin completed the first crewed Moon landing.
explanation: Apollo 11's lunar module Eagle landed in the Sea of Tranquility. Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon several hours later, followed by Buzz Aldrin.

title: The first Earth Day is held
clues: This coordinated action brought environmental concerns into public view.
Millions of people joined teach-ins, rallies, and community events.
The idea was promoted by US senator Gaylord Nelson.
Its success helped build support for modern environmental law.
The first Earth Day was observed across the United States.
explanation: Around 20 million Americans participated in the first Earth Day, a nationwide demonstration that helped establish environmentalism as a major public movement.

sources.label: EarthDay.org — The history of Earth Day

title: The first commercial barcode is scanned
clues: This small transaction changed retail and inventory systems worldwide.
A supermarket checkout in Ohio was the setting.
The item cost 67 cents and was chosen from a multipack.
A Universal Product Code passed over a laser scanner.
A pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit gum became the first retail barcode scan.
explanation: A cashier at Marsh Supermarket in Troy, Ohio scanned a pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit gum, completing the first commercial UPC transaction.

title: Viking 1 lands on Mars
clues: This mission returned the first long-running observations from another planet's surface.
Its landing site was a plain called Chryse Planitia.
The craft carried cameras, weather instruments, and biology experiments.
It transmitted the first clear close-up images from the Martian ground.
NASA's Viking 1 made a successful soft landing on Mars.
explanation: Viking 1 landed in Chryse Planitia and began a six-year mission studying the Martian surface and atmosphere.

title: Star Wars opens in cinemas
clues: This film release reshaped blockbuster cinema and visual effects.
It initially opened in fewer than 50 theaters.
Its story drew on serial adventures, mythology, and samurai films.
Audiences met Luke Skywalker, Princess Leia, and Darth Vader.
George Lucas's original Star Wars opened in the United States.
explanation: Star Wars opened in US theaters and grew into a global hit, transforming popular cinema and launching a long-running franchise.

title: The first baby conceived through IVF is born
clues: This birth demonstrated a new treatment for infertility.
The medical technique joined egg and sperm outside the body.
The pregnancy was closely monitored in northern England.
Doctors Robert Edwards and Patrick Steptoe led the pioneering work.
Louise Brown, the first baby conceived through IVF, was born.
explanation: Louise Brown was born in Oldham, England, becoming the first person conceived through in vitro fertilization.

sources.label: Nobel Prize — Robert Edwards and IVF

title: The world declares smallpox eradicated
clues: This announcement marked an unmatched public-health achievement.
A global vaccination campaign had tracked outbreaks country by country.
The last naturally occurring case had been recorded several years earlier.
It remains the only human infectious disease eradicated worldwide.
The World Health Assembly declared smallpox eradicated.
explanation: The World Health Assembly formally accepted the conclusion that smallpox had been eradicated, ending a disease that had affected humanity for millennia.

title: IBM introduces its personal computer
clues: This product helped establish a standard for business and home computing.
It used components from multiple outside suppliers.
Its operating system came from a young company led by Bill Gates.
The machine's model number was 5150.
IBM introduced the IBM Personal Computer.
explanation: IBM launched the model 5150 Personal Computer, whose open architecture helped define the dominant PC platform.

sources.label: IBM — The birth of the IBM PC

title: Apple introduces the Macintosh
clues: This launch brought a graphical interface to a wider consumer audience.
A famous television commercial had aired two days earlier.
The computer used a mouse and displayed icons on a desktop.
Steve Jobs demonstrated the machine to shareholders in California.
Apple introduced the original Macintosh.
explanation: Steve Jobs unveiled the original Macintosh, promoting a graphical user interface and mouse as a more approachable way to use a personal computer.

title: The Berlin Wall opens
clues: This event transformed the political map of Europe.
It followed weeks of public demonstrations and political change.
A confused press conference made new travel rules sound immediately effective.
Crowds gathered at checkpoints separating East and West.
Border guards opened crossings through the Berlin Wall.
explanation: After an East German official announced relaxed travel rules, crowds gathered at Berlin checkpoints and guards opened the border, beginning the Wall's fall.

sources.label: German government — Fall of the Berlin Wall

title: Nelson Mandela is released from prison
clues: This release became a turning point in a country's democratic transition.
The prisoner had spent 27 years in custody.
Much of that time was served on Robben Island.
He walked free from Victor Verster Prison with Winnie Mandela.
Nelson Mandela was released as apartheid negotiations gathered pace.
explanation: Nelson Mandela left Victor Verster Prison after 27 years in custody, a pivotal moment in the negotiations that ended apartheid.

sources.label: Nelson Mandela Foundation — Release from prison

title: The first website goes online
clues: This publication opened a new way to share linked information globally.
It ran on a NeXT computer at a European physics laboratory.
The page explained how to create and browse documents using a new system.
Its address began with info.cern.ch.
Tim Berners-Lee made the first World Wide Web site publicly available.
explanation: Tim Berners-Lee announced the World Wide Web project and made its first website at CERN available to the wider internet.

sources.label: CERN — The original World Wide Web project

title: The first SMS text message is sent
clues: This short message previewed a new everyday form of communication.
It traveled from a computer to a mobile telephone.
The recipient worked for the British network Vodafone.
The message contained only two seasonal words.
Engineer Neil Papworth sent the text Merry Christmas.
explanation: Neil Papworth sent Merry Christmas from a computer to Vodafone director Richard Jarvis's mobile phone, completing the first SMS message.

title: Nelson Mandela is inaugurated as president
clues: This ceremony completed a historic democratic transition.
It followed the country's first election with universal adult suffrage.
Dignitaries from around the world gathered in Pretoria.
The new leader had spent 27 years as a political prisoner.
Nelson Mandela became South Africa's first Black president.
explanation: Nelson Mandela was inaugurated as president of South Africa in Pretoria after the country's first fully democratic national election.

title: Deep Blue defeats Garry Kasparov
clues: This contest became a milestone in the public story of artificial intelligence.
A world champion faced a specialized machine across six games.
The decisive match took place in New York City.
The computer could evaluate millions of chess positions each second.
IBM's Deep Blue defeated chess champion Garry Kasparov in the final game.
explanation: Deep Blue won the sixth and final game of its rematch with Garry Kasparov, becoming the first computer to defeat a reigning world chess champion in a match.

title: The first International Space Station module launches
clues: This launch began construction of a permanent laboratory in orbit.
The project joined agencies from the United States, Russia, Europe, Japan, and Canada.
Its first component provided power, propulsion, and storage.
The Russian-built module was named Zarya, meaning sunrise.
A Proton rocket launched the first module of the International Space Station.
explanation: The Zarya control module launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome, marking the start of on-orbit assembly of the International Space Station.

title: The first draft of the human genome is announced
clues: This scientific milestone produced a new map of human biology.
Researchers across several countries worked on the project for years.
The effort read billions of chemical letters stored in DNA.
Public and private teams announced their draft results together.
Leaders presented the first working draft of the human genome sequence.
explanation: The Human Genome Project and Celera Genomics jointly announced working drafts covering most of the human genome, a landmark for genetics and medicine.

sources.label: National Human Genome Research Institute — Timeline

title: Wikipedia launches
clues: This project changed how people create and consult reference material online.
Its articles could be written and edited collaboratively by volunteers.
It began as a companion to a more traditional expert-written encyclopedia.
The site's software and open model allowed it to grow quickly in many languages.
Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger launched Wikipedia.
explanation: Wikipedia went online as a freely editable encyclopedia and grew into one of the world's most widely used reference websites.

title: The first YouTube video is uploaded
clues: This short upload began a platform that transformed online video.
The clip lasts less than 20 seconds.
It was recorded at the San Diego Zoo.
A co-founder briefly comments on elephants and their trunks.
Jawed Karim uploaded Me at the zoo to YouTube.
explanation: YouTube co-founder Jawed Karim uploaded Me at the zoo, the first video published on the platform.

title: Pluto is reclassified as a dwarf planet
clues: This vote changed a scientific category familiar from school textbooks.
Astronomers had discovered several similar bodies in the outer Solar System.
A new definition required an object to clear its orbital neighborhood.
The decision was made at an international astronomy meeting in Prague.
The International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet.
explanation: The International Astronomical Union adopted a formal definition of a planet that placed Pluto in the new dwarf-planet category.

title: Apple unveils the iPhone
clues: This product announcement reshaped mobile computing.
The presenter described three devices before revealing they were one product.
Its interface centered on a large multi-touch screen.
The demonstration took place at Macworld in San Francisco.
Steve Jobs introduced Apple's first iPhone.
explanation: Steve Jobs unveiled the original iPhone at Macworld, combining a phone, widescreen media player, and internet communicator in one touch-driven device.

sources.label: Apple Newsroom — Apple reinvents the phone

title: Scientists announce evidence of the Higgs boson
clues: This announcement filled a major gap in the leading theory of particle physics.
Two independent experiments reported a new particle at the same laboratory.
The evidence came from collisions inside a 27-kilometre ring.
The particle was associated with a field that gives other particles mass.
CERN announced the discovery of a particle consistent with the Higgs boson.
explanation: The ATLAS and CMS experiments at CERN announced a new particle consistent with the long-predicted Higgs boson, later confirmed through further measurements.

title: Curiosity lands on Mars
clues: This mission placed a mobile science laboratory on another planet.
Its landing sequence was nicknamed seven minutes of terror.
A rocket-powered sky crane lowered the vehicle on cables.
The destination was Gale Crater near a mountain later called Mount Sharp.
NASA's Curiosity rover landed successfully on Mars.
explanation: The Curiosity rover landed inside Gale Crater using an innovative sky-crane system and began investigating whether Mars once had habitable environments.

title: The Paris Agreement is adopted
clues: This agreement created a shared framework for addressing a global environmental threat.
Nearly every country took part in the negotiations.
Governments committed to submit and strengthen national climate plans.
A central aim was to keep warming well below two degrees Celsius.
Delegates at COP21 adopted the Paris climate agreement.
explanation: Parties to the UN climate convention adopted the Paris Agreement, committing countries to collective action on greenhouse-gas emissions and climate resilience.

title: The first image of a black hole is released
clues: This image made an invisible astronomical object visible through its surroundings.
Observatories across Earth worked together like one planet-sized telescope.
The result showed a bright ring around a dark central shadow.
The subject lies at the center of the galaxy Messier 87.
The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration released the first image of a black hole.
explanation: The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration revealed the first direct image of a black hole's shadow, captured in the galaxy Messier 87.

title: The James Webb Space Telescope launches
clues: This observatory was built to look deeper into cosmic history.
Its segmented primary mirror is coated with a thin layer of gold.
A large sunshield had to unfold after launch.
The telescope traveled toward a point roughly 1.5 million kilometres from Earth.
An Ariane 5 rocket launched the James Webb Space Telescope.
explanation: The James Webb Space Telescope launched from French Guiana, beginning its journey to the Sun-Earth L2 point and a new era of infrared astronomy.

title: Chandrayaan-3 lands near the Moon's south pole
clues: This mission achieved a first in a challenging region of the Moon.
It followed an earlier landing attempt by the same national space agency.
The mission included a lander named Vikram and a rover named Pragyan.
Its success made its country the fourth to complete a soft lunar landing.
India's Chandrayaan-3 landed near the lunar south pole.
explanation: The Chandrayaan-3 lander Vikram touched down near the lunar south pole, making India the fourth country to achieve a soft landing on the Moon.
